definition: A reasoning framework that generalizes chain-of-thought by letting a model explore, evaluate, and backtrack across multiple possible reasoning paths structured as a tree.
details: Tree of Thoughts allows models to perform lookahead and self-evaluation across branching reasoning paths, improving performance on problems requiring search or planning, such as puzzles.

explainer.lead: Tree of Thoughts is a reasoning framework that generalizes chain-of-thought by letting a model explore, evaluate and backtrack across multiple reasoning paths arranged as a tree. It matters because lookahead and self-evaluation improve results on problems requiring search or planning.

tiers.eli5: Instead of walking one straight path to an answer, the model tries several branches, checks them, and backs up when a branch looks wrong.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it for puzzles and planning tasks where a single reasoning chain fails, letting the model self-evaluate branches.
tiers.paperLevel: Tree of Thoughts extends chain-of-thought by structuring reasoning as a tree, allowing lookahead and self-evaluation across branching paths; it improves performance on problems requiring search or planning, such as puzzles.

explainer.example: On a puzzle, the model proposes several partial solutions, scores them, and abandons the weak branches to continue from the promising ones.

citation.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
